BurnBot builds remotely operated wildfire and prescribed-fire machines, combining robotics, engineering, and fire-practice expertise. The entry-level Software Engineer will work across autonomy tooling, backend services, operator interfaces, and data pipelines, owning features, tooling, tests, field data triage, and software issues on real machines with mentorship from senior engineers.

Responsibilities
Features end to end, with a senior engineer alongside you — design, build, review, ship
Tooling and tests that make everyone else faster. This is how you learn the system
Field data triage: something looked wrong on a burn yesterday, and you’ll help figure out what
Real bugs on real machines, which is the fastest engineering education available

Curiosity and comfort with ambiguity
B.S. in computer science or a related field, or equivalent self-taught experience
Applicants must have current, unrestricted work authorization in the United States and must not require employer sponsorship for employment-based visa status, now or in the future
Preferred

Machine learning or computer vision projects
Geospatial or mapping work
Anything you built for a physical device
An interest in wildfire, forestry, or climate work

Flexible paid time off
Work the hours where you’re sharpest, and go remote on heads-down days.
You’ll work across the stack with a mentor.
